options.content: Software for creating and publishing web content without HTML
options.rationale: Correct: content is edited through a dashboard.

options.content: A program that converts high-level code into machine code
options.rationale: That is a translator.

options.content: A device that connects a school network to the internet
options.rationale: That is a router.

options.content: A file that lists the newest posts on a website
options.rationale: That is a web feed.

explanation: A CMS stores content in a database and publishes it through a theme, edited from a browser dashboard.

stem: In a CMS, what is a **plugin**?

options.content: An add-on that gives the site a new feature
options.rationale: Correct: e.g. a contact form or gallery.

options.content: A design package that controls colours and layout
options.rationale: That is a theme.

options.content: A user who is allowed to edit posts
options.rationale: That is an editor role.

options.content: The cable that links the web server to the internet
options.rationale: Plugins are software.

explanation: Plugins (extensions) add features; themes change the look.

stem: Which image format is best for a photograph on a web page?

options.content: GIF
options.rationale: GIF supports only 256 colours; it suits simple graphics and animation.

options.content: SVG
options.rationale: SVG is for vector graphics such as logos and icons.

options.content: JPEG
options.rationale: Correct: lossy compression keeps photo files small.

options.content: Uncompressed bitmap
options.rationale: Far too large for the web.

explanation: JPEG gives small files for photos with millions of colours.

stem: Why can a CMS site change its whole appearance without retyping its content?

options.content: Every page of the site is saved as a single picture
options.rationale: Pages are built from content and theme.

options.content: The content is stored separately from the theme that controls the design
options.rationale: Correct: switching theme re-presents the same content.

options.content: The visitor's browser chooses a new design for each visitor
options.rationale: The design comes from the theme on the server.

options.content: Plugins automatically retype the content
options.rationale: Plugins add features; they do not retype content.

explanation: Separating content (database) from design (theme) is the key idea of a CMS.

options.content: A way for visitors to pay for goods on the website
options.rationale: That is an e-commerce plugin.

options.content: A backup copy of the site's database
options.rationale: That is a backup plugin.

options.content: A theme that rearranges its layout to work on phones
options.rationale: That is a responsive theme.

options.content: An automatically updated list of the newest content for subscribers
options.rationale: Correct: readers see new posts without visiting.

explanation: Feed readers and other sites use the feed to show new posts as they appear.

stem: A school logo with sharp edges must sit on coloured backgrounds without a white box around it. Which format is most suitable?

options.content: JPEG
options.rationale: Lossy compression blurs sharp edges and JPEG has no transparency.

options.content: MP4
options.rationale: MP4 is a video format.

options.content: A plain text file
options.rationale: A text file cannot store an image.

options.content: PNG
options.rationale: Correct: lossless with transparency (SVG would also suit a vector logo).

explanation: PNG is lossless and supports transparent backgrounds.
hints: Which format keeps sharp edges and allows a transparent background?

stem: Why must a CMS and its plugins be kept updated?

options.content: Old versions delete all the posts that are more than a year old
options.rationale: Posts are not deleted by age.

options.content: Updates make every image smaller
options.rationale: Image size depends on optimisation.

options.content: Updates fix security weaknesses that hackers could exploit
options.rationale: Correct: popular CMSs are common targets.

options.content: The theme stops displaying colours unless it is updated
options.rationale: Colour display is not the reason.

explanation: Out-of-date plugins and CMS cores are a common way into websites.

stem: Tatenda has installed 40 plugins on his small club website and it has become slow. What is the best advice?

options.content: Install another plugin to fix each new problem as it appears
options.rationale: More plugins usually make it slower.

options.content: Change the colour of the theme
options.rationale: Colour does not affect speed.

options.content: Upload all the photos at their full camera size instead
options.rationale: This would slow the site further.

options.content: Remove plugins that are not needed and keep the rest updated
options.rationale: Correct: each plugin adds code to load and a possible security risk.

explanation: Fewer, updated plugins make a site faster and more secure.
hints: Think about what each plugin costs in speed and security.

stem: A theme changes how a CMS website looks, whereas a plugin adds what it can do.
explanation: True. Themes control design; plugins add features.

stem: Authors must know HTML before they can add a post to a CMS website.
explanation: False. A CMS provides an editor in the dashboard, so authors can add content without HTML.

stem: An uncompressed photo is 640 × 480 pixels, stored with 3 bytes per pixel. Calculate its size in KB, where 1 KB = 1024 bytes.
A 1600 × 1200 pixel image (24-bit colour) is 5625 KB uncompressed. Rudo resizes it to 800 × 600 pixels. What is the new uncompressed size in KB?
explanation: Halving both dimensions gives a quarter of the pixels: 5625 ÷ 4 = 1406.25 KB.
hints: Halving both sides divides the number of pixels by four.

stem: Match each CMS plugin to what it adds.

right.content: Help with page titles and descriptions for search engines
Scheduled copies of the database and files
Products, a shopping basket and payment
A form whose answers are emailed to the owner

payload.template: The design package that controls the layout and colours of a CMS site is a {{blank:a}}. A {{blank:b}} theme rearranges the layout to suit phone and computer screens. Small blocks such as a calendar placed in a side bar are called {{blank:c}}.

stem: Describe **three** steps to optimise a photograph before uploading it to a website. [3]

points.description: Resize to the largest size at which it will be displayed
Save in a suitable format (JPEG) and compress it / add a meaningful file name and alt text

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Crop away the parts that are not needed, resize it to the width it will be shown at, and save it as a compressed JPEG.

explanation: Crop, resize, choose format and compress.
hints: Think about the steps before uploading.

stem: A youth club in Bulawayo is deciding whether to build its website with a CMS or by writing HTML by hand. Give **two** advantages and **two** disadvantages of using a CMS. [4]

points.description: Advantage: members can add content without knowing HTML / several users with roles
Advantage: quick to set up with ready-made themes and plugins / consistent design
Disadvantage: security risks if the CMS or plugins are not updated / common target for hackers
Disadvantage: less control over the code / can be slow with many plugins / needs a server with a database

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Members can update the site without HTML and it is quick to set up with themes and plugins. However, it must be kept updated to stay secure, and the club has less control over the code, which can become slow with many plugins.

stem: Chipo is building a website for her family's lodge near Victoria Falls using a CMS.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe how the CMS produces a page when a visitor requests it.

points.description: The content is retrieved from the database
It is placed into the theme's layout and sent to the browser as HTML

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The CMS takes the page's content from its database, places it into the theme's layout and sends the resulting HTML to the visitor's browser.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Which would let guests book rooms on the site?

options.content: A new colour scheme
options.rationale: Only changes the look.

options.content: A booking (e-commerce) plugin
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: A larger logo
options.rationale: Only changes the look.

options.content: A web feed
options.rationale: Lists new posts.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Which format should she use for photos of the lodge?

options.content: GIF
options.rationale: Few colours.

options.content: JPEG
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: SVG
options.rationale: For vector graphics.

options.content: MP4
options.rationale: Video format.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why she should resize the photos before uploading them.

points.description: Smaller image dimensions mean smaller files
Pages load faster / use less of visitors' mobile data / less storage space

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Resizing reduces the number of pixels and so the file size, so pages load faster and use less of visitors' data.

explanation: Database + theme → HTML; plugins add booking; JPEG; resize for speed.
hints: Content in the database, design in the theme.
JPEG for photos, PNG for transparency.

stem: A Masvingo community radio station (fictional) uses a CMS for its news website.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Classify each change as needing a theme or a plugin.

left.content: Changing the menu from the top to the side
Using the station's colours and fonts

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain how a web feed helps the station's regular readers.

points.description: The feed lists new stories automatically as they are published
Readers' feed apps / other sites show the new stories without the reader visiting the site to check

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The feed lists each new story as it is published, so readers' feed apps show it without them having to visit the site.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Give **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of placing adverts on the site.

points.description: Advantage: earns income for the station
Disadvantage: annoys visitors / slows the page / less space for content

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Adverts earn money for the station, but too many annoy visitors and slow pages down.

explanation: Themes vs plugins; feeds push new content; adverts bring income but cost speed.
hints: Adverts earn money but can annoy visitors.
